definitions.rationale: This rule is the macro expansion of the named AnyIntCall proof term into the ordinary source-level call through Name("any_int"); it defines syntax and adds no mathematical or operational fact.
definitions.text:
rule AnyIntCall(X:Val, Y:Val, Z:Val)
    => Call(Name("any_int"), (X, Y, Z))

definitions.rationale: This rule is the macro expansion of anyIntModuleScope into the loaded module scope containing the exact function closure, so it structurally defines a named proof configuration.
definitions.text:
rule anyIntModuleScope
    => scope(
         "any_int" |->
           closureVal(
             ("x", "y", "z"),
             Return(
               BoolOp(
                 "and",
                 ( Call(Name("isinstance"), (Name("x"), Name("int")))
                 , Call(Name("isinstance"), (Name("y"), Name("int")))
                 , Call(Name("isinstance"), (Name("z"), Name("int")))
                 , BoolOp(
                     "or",
                     ( Compare(BinOp("+", Name("x"), Name("y")), CmpOp("==", Name("z")))
                     , Compare(BinOp("+", Name("x"), Name("z")), CmpOp("==", Name("y")))
                     , Compare(BinOp("+", Name("y"), Name("z")), CmpOp("==", Name("x")))
                     )
                   )
                 )
               )
             ) .Stmts,
             0
           ),
         parent(-1)
       )

definitions.rationale: This equation defines the total mathematical summary anySum directly as the three integer sum-equality cases used by the postcondition.
definitions.text:
rule anySum(X:Int, Y:Int, Z:Int)
    => ((X +Int Y) ==Int Z)
       orBool ((X +Int Z) ==Int Y)
       orBool ((Y +Int Z) ==Int X)

source_rules.rationale: This simplification rule adds a reusable symbolic equality for the imported boolAsInt function; Stage 1 compiles it into the proof definition before kprove and never first proves its exact statement in a module that excludes it.
